parameters.description: Only this owner's jobs

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: Only this API key's jobs (key-scoped attribution)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, clamped to 1..=100 (default 20)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset from the previous page's next_cursor

200.description: One page of jobs with the creating key's prefix

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user)

422.description: Tampered cursor, bad limit, or malformed uuid filter

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/plans (P1-056): the plan catalog for the
editor — all plans, cheapest first, with the parsed
entitlements (the same seven keys the profile and the
quota middleware read). Admin + support (the read-only
role) may call it; a verified plain user gets 403
`PF-1002` from the extractor, no credential gets 401
`PF-1001`.

200.description: The plan catalog, cheapest first

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user)

put.summary:
PUT /v1/admin/plans (P1-056): batch-edit the catalog —
per-plan updates (`plans`, keyed by `code`) plus the
codes to delete (`remove`). Admin only; support gets 403
`PF-1002` from the extractor, no credential gets 401
`PF-1001`. A malformed or invalid edit is 422 `PF-2002`
(with `field_errors`); an unknown plan code is 404
`PF-2010`; removing a plan with subscriptions is 409
`PF-2012`. The whole PUT applies in one transaction, so
a blocked removal rolls the updates back too. On success
the catalog cache is invalidated before the response is
built, so the returned catalog is the fresh one; the
write is audited by the P1-046 middleware
(`admin.plans.updated`) with the changed codes attached
as the audit `after` — the handler does NOT mark
`AuditHandled`.

200.description: The updated catalog, cheapest first

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin, incl. support)

409.description: Plan has subscriptions and cannot be removed

422.description: Invalid edit (entitlements, price, currency, Stripe price id, or the free-plan rules)

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/usage/{id} (P1-081): the admin usage
view — the P1-080 shape for an arbitrary user (today +
the 30-day window ending today from the durable
`usage_counters` rows) plus the all-time totals and
today's per-key breakdown (always present here — an
admin sees everything). Admin + support (the read-only
role) may call it; a verified plain user gets 403
`PF-1002` from the extractor, no credential gets 401
`PF-1001`, an API key gets 403. A user who does not
exist is 404 `PF-2010`; a user who exists but used
nothing gets zeros, not a 404. No audit row (a read
creates nothing).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Whose usage to view

200.description: The user's usage: today, the 30-day window, the all-time totals, and today's per-key breakdown

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user, or an API key)

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/usage/{id}/export (P1-081): the same
30-day window as CSV, for billing disputes — one header
row (`date,images,video_seconds`) plus one row per day,
oldest first. Admin + support may call it; a verified
plain user gets 403 `PF-1002` from the extractor, no
credential gets 401 `PF-1001`, an API key gets 403. A
user who does not exist is 404 `PF-2010`; a user who
exists but used nothing gets the header plus 30 zero
rows, not a 404. The response is `text/csv` with a
`Content-Disposition: attachment` filename, so a browser
downloads it instead of rendering it. No audit row (a
read creates nothing).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Whose usage to export

200.description: The user's 30-day usage as CSV: header date,images,video_seconds plus one row per day, oldest first

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user, or an API key)

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/users (P1-009): search users. Admin +
support (the read-only role) may call it; a verified plain
user gets 403 `PF-1002` from the extractor, no credential
gets 401 `PF-1001`. Answers the api-spec pagination shape
(`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` — `next_cursor`
omitted on the last page). A tampered cursor is 422
`PF-2002`; a non-numeric `limit` is rejected by the `Query`
extractor the same way (the error mapper rewrites the
framework 400 to the 422 problem).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Prefix filter on email, display name, or id (case-insensitive); blank lists everything

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, clamped to 1..=100 (default 20)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset from the previous page's next_cursor

200.description: One page of users

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user)

422.description: Tampered cursor or bad limit

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/users/lookup (P1-109): the user lookup
helper — resolve a user from whatever identifier a
support ticket carries (`?email=…` / `?id=…` /
`?job_id=…`, exactly one) and return the P1-106 support
view. Admin + support (the read-only role) may call it;
a verified plain user gets 403 `PF-1002` from the
extractor, no credential gets 401 `PF-1001`, an API key
gets 403. Exactly one key (zero or 2+ is 422 `PF-2002`,
all failures collected; email must parse as an email,
`id` / `job_id` as UUIDs; unknown query keys are 422).
A key that resolves to no user is 404 `PF-2010`. Every
lookup audits as `admin.users.lookup` — including misses
(a 404 still writes one row, so a probing pattern is
visible) — and no raw searched value is stored in the
audit row. Denials (401/403) and validation failures
(422) audit nothing. No state change, no provider call,
no mail. The service wrote the audit row, so the handler
marks `AuditHandled` and the P1-046 middleware stands
down — the row exists exactly once (the route is
deliberately NOT in `audit_action_for`: the middleware's
contract is writes).

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Resolve by email (case-insensitive); exactly one of email, id, job_id

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Resolve by user id (UUID); exactly one of email, id, job_id

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Resolve by job id (UUID) through the job's owner; exactly one of email, id, job_id

200.description: The user's support view: profile, plan, usage, recent jobs, and live sessions

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user, or an API key)

404.description: No such user (or no such job for job_id)

422.description: Zero or two-or-more keys, a malformed email or UUID, or an unknown query key

500.description: The lookup read or audit write failed

get.summary:
GET /v1/admin/users/{id} (P1-106): the support user
view — profile, plan, usage, recent jobs, session meta
for one user. Admin + support (the read-only role) may
call it; a verified plain user gets 403 `PF-1002` from
the extractor, no credential gets 401 `PF-1001`, an API
key gets 403. A user who does not exist is 404 `PF-2010`;
a user who exists but has no subscription is Free, no
jobs or no live sessions is empty arrays, not a 404. No
secrets anywhere in the shape (ADR-0065): no password
hash, no refresh hash, no provider ids. No audit row (a
read creates nothing).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Whose view to read

200.description: The user's support view: profile, plan, usage, recent jobs, and live sessions

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified plain user, or an API key)

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/impersonate (P1-010): mint a
15-minute scoped token that acts as the target user. Admin
only (support may not impersonate — it is a write, and the
`AdminContext` extractor rejects support with 403
`PF-1002`). The token carries `impersonator_id` in its
claims; it has no refresh and no session row, so it dies
at `exp`. Returns the token + the two ids the console
needs for the banner.

200.description: Scoped impersonation token (15 min)

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin, incl. support)

422.description: Reason missing, blank, too long, or with control characters

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/notes (P1-110): append a ticket
note to a user's append-only list. The note and its
`admin.users.note_added` audit row commit in one
transaction, and the response carries `AuditHandled` so
the P1-046 middleware stands down and the row exists
exactly once. The audit row carries the note id + the
body length only — no verbatim body (the note lives in
exactly one place: the column). The list is append-only
twice over: one repo fn appends, and the
`users_support_notes_append_only` trigger raises on any
UPDATE that drops or rewrites an element. Support reads
the notes through the P1-106 view (a sixth section), not
through this endpoint. Returns the full list after the
append with 200 — an admin action on a user answers 200
(the suspend/warn/grant precedent), not 201, even though
a note is created. Admin-only — support is read-only.

200.description: Appended; the full note list after the append

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin, or an API key)

422.description: Body missing, blank, over 2000 characters, or with control characters

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/quota-grant (P1-107): a manual,
expiring quota bump — extra daily images and/or
video-seconds for `ttl_hours` (1–168), with a reason. The
grant and its `admin.users.quota_granted` audit row commit
in one transaction, and the response carries
`AuditHandled` so the P1-046 middleware stands down and
the row exists exactly once. The bump is honored by the
quota snapshot (the pre-check, the profile, and the quota
warnings all read the same limits), and it stops counting
the moment `expires_at` passes. Returns the created grant
with 200 — an admin action on a user answers 200 (the
suspend/warn precedent; the authz live walk pins 200 for
every live admin write except the catalog sync), not 201,
even though a row is created. Admin-only — support is
read-only.

200.description: Granted

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin, or an API key)

422.description: No amount, a non-positive amount, ttl_hours outside 1..=168, or a bad reason

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/restore (P1-008): restore a
suspended account. Status becomes `active`, held jobs are
released back to `queued`, and the action is audited
(`user.restored`, actor = the admin). Sessions stay revoked
(the user logs in again). Idempotent: restoring a
non-suspended account is a 200 no-op. Returns the updated
user.

200.description: Restored (or not suspended)

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin)

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/suspend (P1-008): suspend the
account with a reason. Status becomes `suspended`, every
live session is revoked, every queued job is held, and the
action is audited (`user.suspended`, actor = the admin).
Idempotent: suspending an already-suspended account is a
200 no-op (no write, no audit). A suspend cancels any
pending deletion (`deleted_at` cleared — the grace does not
survive admin intervention). Returns the updated user.

200.description: Suspended (or already suspended)

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin)

422.description: Reason missing, blank, too long, or with control characters

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/terminate (P1-091): the
ladder's third rung — termination with a reason. Status
becomes `deletion_pending` (the P1-007 grace: purge
after 30 days), every live session is revoked, every
queued job is held, and the action is audited
(`user.terminated`, actor = the admin) with the
`enforcement-termination` mail enqueued in the same
transaction. Requires a `suspended` account — the ladder
is sequential, an active account cannot be terminated
outright (422). Idempotent: terminating an
already-terminated account is a 200 no-op (no write, no
audit, no mail). A terminated account cannot log in
(403 `PF-1004`) — the login does NOT cancel an
admin-initiated termination the way it cancels a
self-requested deletion. Returns the user + the rung
that ran.

200.description: Terminated (or already terminated)

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin)

422.description: Reason missing, blank, too long, or with control characters; or the account is not suspended

post.summary:
POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/warn (P1-091): the ladder's
first rung — a formal warning with a reason. The status
does not change; the warning is audited (`user.warned`,
actor = the admin) and the `enforcement-warning` mail
is enqueued in the same transaction. A warning is
repeatable: each call is a new warning event. Requires
an `active` account — warning a suspended or
deletion-pending one is 422 (the ladder only moves
forward). Returns the user + the rung that ran.

200.description: Warned

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: Forbidden (verified non-admin)

422.description: Reason missing, blank, too long, or with control characters; or the account is not active

post.summary:
Mint an API key (P1-033, FR-A-06): `pf_live_` + 24 random
bytes, sha256 stored, full secret shown once in this
response. Max 10 live keys per user — the 11th is 409
`PF-2011` (Conflict: the request is valid, the user's
state refuses it). P1-055 (FR-P-01): the caller's plan
must grant the `api_keys` feature — a Free user is 403
`PF-3003`, after validation (a malformed request stays
422) and before the cap.

201.description: Key created; the full secret is shown here once and never again

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

403.description: Plan does not include API keys (PF-3003)

422.description: Invalid name or scopes (PF-2002)

delete.summary:
Revoke an API key (P1-036, FR-A-06): `DELETE
/v1/api-keys/{id}` stamps `revoked_at` and denylists the
key's hash — the key dies immediately (its next use is 401
`PF-1001`) and stops counting toward the 10-live-keys cap.
204 No Content, no body. A key cannot revoke (itself or
any other): the route is not in the extractor's scope
table, so a key caller is 403 `PF-1002` before this
handler runs. Unknown id or another user's id are 404
`PF-2010` (no enumeration); re-revoking your own dead key
is a no-op 204 (DELETE is idempotent — the P1-019 session
convention).

204.description: Key revoked; the secret dies immediately

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

403.description: An API key cannot revoke (PF-1002)

404.description: Unknown id or another user's key (PF-2010)

post.summary:
Rotate an API key (P1-035, FR-A-06): `POST
/v1/api-keys/{id}/rotate` mints a replacement secret
(same name + scopes) and keeps the old secret valid for
the overlap window (`PF_API_KEY_ROTATION_OVERLAP_SECS`,
default 24 h). The response carries the NEW secret once —
the same shape as creation; the old secret is never
shown again. A key cannot rotate (itself or any other):
the route is not in the extractor's scope table, so a
key caller is 403 `PF-1002` before this handler runs.
Unknown id, another user's id, or a revoked key are all
404 `PF-2010` (no enumeration).

201.description: Key rotated; the new secret is shown here once and never again

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

403.description: An API key cannot rotate (PF-1002)

404.description: Unknown id, another user's key, or a revoked key (PF-2010)

post.summary:
Confirm an email change (P1-006, FR-A-01): consume the
`email_change` token from the confirmation link mailed to
the NEW address, swap the email to the pending address
(clearing the intent, verifying the new address). Unknown /
used / wrong-purpose token → 401 PF-1010; expired token →
401 PF-1011; an address taken by another account while it
was pending → 409 PF-2011. Success is 204 (no body —
the client re-reads the profile with GET /v1/me).

204.description: Email swapped to the pending address; new address verified

401.description: Invalid or expired token

409.description: Pending address taken by another account meanwhile

422.description: Validation failed (token required)

post.summary:
Request a password reset (P1-025, FR-A-01). 204-always:
a known email, an unknown email, and an already-… — all
answer 204 with an empty body; only the rate-limit 429
(PF-3007, the reset-account bucket — identical for known
and unknown addresses) and a 500 vary the response. No
enumeration, by construction.

204.description: If the email is registered, a reset mail was queued (always 204 — no enumeration)

422.description: Validation failed (email shape)

429.description: Too many reset attempts for this email (PF-3007, Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* trio)

post.summary:
Log a user in (P1-003, FR-A-01). Thin handler: the service
owns the flow; this maps its errors to the problem+json
envelope and sets the refresh cookie. Returns `Response`
directly (the P1-001 handler shape — clippy
`result_large_err` forbids `Result<_, ProblemResponse>`).
post.description:
The device info comes from the request itself: the
`User-Agent` header and the socket address
(`MaybeConnectInfo` — the never-rejecting extractor; oneshot
tests have no socket, so the IP is `"unknown"` there). No
XFF: the device record is the socket IP, not a spoofable
header.

200.description: Logged in; access token in the body, refresh token in the httpOnly cookie

401.description: Invalid email or password (generic — no enumeration)

422.description: Validation failed (email shape, password required)

429.description: Too many login attempts for this account

post.summary:
Log out of the presented session (P1-017, FR-A-01). Thin
handler: the service owns the flow; this maps its errors
to the problem+json envelope and clears the refresh
cookie. The session is the one behind the `detag_refresh`
cookie — there is no body, and a Bearer token alone
cannot log one session out (the access token carries no
session identity; its `jti` is per-issuance, not linked
to a session row). No cookie, or an unknown hash → the
generic 401 `PF-1001` (the lookup must not say whether
the session existed). Logging out twice is a no-op 204
(the session is already dead — P1-008's convention).

204.description: Presented session revoked; the refresh cookie is cleared

401.description: No cookie, or unknown refresh token (PF-1001, generic)

post.summary:
Log out of every session (P1-017, FR-A-01). Thin handler:
the service owns the flow; this maps its errors to the
problem+json envelope and clears the refresh cookie. The
caller is the Bearer `AuthContext` — the access token
identifies the USER (not the session), so the only safe
scope is every session. A cookie-only caller gets 401
`PF-1001` (the extractor rejects a bare cookie — P1-016):
the web client sends both (Bearer in memory + the cookie
the browser attaches), an API client sends the Bearer,
and a caller with only the cookie uses `POST
/v1/auth/logout` for the single session.

204.description: Every session revoked; the refresh cookie is cleared

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

post.summary:
Refresh the access token (P1-014, FR-A-01). Thin handler:
the service owns the flow; this maps its errors to the
problem+json envelope and sets the new refresh cookie.
The refresh token comes from the `detag_refresh` cookie
only — there is no body (a client that lost the cookie
logs in again). The device info is built the same way as
login (the `User-Agent` header + the socket address;
oneshot tests have no socket, so the IP is `"unknown"`
there). An impersonation token in the cookie is not a
refresh token — there is no session row behind it, so the
hash lookup fails with the same generic 401 (P1-010's
promise: P1-014's refresh rejects it).

200.description: Rotated; new access token in the body, new refresh token in the httpOnly cookie

401.description: No cookie, or unknown / revoked / expired refresh token (PF-1001, generic); a rotated token reused is PF-1007 (whole family revoked)

post.summary:
Register a user (P1-001, FR-A-01). Thin handler: the
service owns the flow; this maps its errors to the
problem+json envelope. Returns `Response` directly (not
`Result<_, ProblemResponse>`): `ProblemResponse` is 152
bytes, and clippy's `result_large_err` (deny) forbids it as
the `Err` of a `Result` whose `Ok` is small — and axum has
no `IntoResponse` for `Box<ProblemResponse>` either. Every
real handler follows this shape; see the adding-an-endpoint
doc.

409.description: Email already registered (generic body — no enumeration detail)

422.description: Validation failed (email shape, password length, ToS version, disposable domain)

429.description: Too many registration attempts for this email (PF-3007, Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* trio)

post.summary:
Re-send a verification mail (P1-002, FR-A-01). This route
is NOT in the original api-spec — the spec says "resend
rate-limited (3/hour)" but names no route. Added as
`POST /v1/auth/resend-verification`, 204-always: unknown
email, already-verified user, and over-limit resends all
answer 204 with no mail (no enumeration, mirroring
forgot-password). Only a 500 varies the response.

204.description: If the email is registered and unverified (and under the hourly limit), a fresh verification mail was queued

422.description: Validation failed (email shape)

post.summary:
Reset the password with a token from the reset link
(P1-025, FR-A-01). Unknown / used / wrong-purpose token
→ 401 PF-1010; expired token → 401 PF-1011. Success is
204 — the password is changed, the lockout counter is
cleared, and EVERY session is revoked (the caller logs in
again with the new password).

401.description: Invalid or expired reset token

422.description: Validation failed (token required, password min 12)

post.summary:
Verify an email (P1-002, FR-A-01): consume the single-use
token from the verification link, set `email_verified_at`.
Unknown/used token → 401 PF-1010; expired token → 401
PF-1011. Success is 204 (no body — nothing to return).

401.description: Invalid or expired token

422.description: Validation failed (token required)

post.summary:
Create a checkout session (P1-062, FR-P-03; proration
P1-069): the buyer is redirected to the provider-hosted
page at the returned `url`. JWT only — the route is not in
the extractor's scope table, so an API key is 403 `PF-1002`
before this handler runs (P1-040's "no billing for keys");
no credential is 401 `PF-1001` from the extractor. The
`Idempotency-Key` header is honored (a replay returns the
stored session, a reuse with a different request is 409
`PF-2011`); without the header every call is a fresh
checkout. Billing not configured is 503 `PF-5005`. A buyer
who already holds a live subscription gets the P1-069
treatment: the same plan is 422, an upgrade returns the
session with a proration preview (200), and a downgrade
returns 202 with the scheduled change — no session, no
provider call.

200.description: The hosted checkout session — redirect the buyer to `url`

202.description: Downgrade scheduled — the change applies at `effective_at`, no session to open

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: An API key cannot check out (PF-1002)

409.description: Idempotency key reused with a different request, or a plan change is already scheduled (PF-2011)

422.description: Invalid body, or the plan cannot be bought (PF-2002)

503.description: Billing is not configured (no Stripe secret key)

get.summary:
List the caller's invoices (P1-068, FR-P-03): newest
first, from the provider, cached 5 minutes per customer.
JWT only — the route is not in the extractor's scope
table, so an API key is 403 `PF-1002` before this handler
runs (P1-040's "no billing for keys"); no credential is
401 `PF-1001` from the extractor. A user with no provider
customer on file gets 200 with an empty list (a list, not
a page to open — the portal's 404 does not apply here);
billing not configured is 503 `PF-5005`.

200.description: The caller's invoices, newest first

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: An API key cannot list invoices (PF-1002)

503.description: Billing is not configured (no Stripe secret key)

post.summary:
Open the billing portal (P1-067, FR-P-03): the caller is
sent to the provider-hosted page at the returned `url` to
manage payment methods, see invoices, and cancel. JWT
only — the route is not in the extractor's scope table, so
an API key is 403 `PF-1002` before this handler runs
(P1-040's "no billing for keys"); no credential is 401
`PF-1001` from the extractor. A user with no provider
customer on file is 404 `PF-2010`; billing not configured
is 503 `PF-5005`.

200.description: The hosted billing-portal session — redirect the buyer to `url`

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: An API key cannot open the portal (PF-1002)

503.description: Billing is not configured (no Stripe secret key)

get.summary:
GET /v1/me (P1-005): the profile + the current plan + today's
quota snapshot. The snapshot is the entitlements service's
reading (plan entitlements vs today's usage row) — the same
two sources the quota middleware (P1-051) reads, so the
snapshot and the middleware agree by construction.

200.description: Profile with plan and quota snapshot

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

delete.summary:
DELETE /v1/me (P1-007): request account deletion. The
account enters the 30-day grace (`status =
'deletion_pending'`, `deleted_at` = now); the nightly purge
hard-deletes it 30 days later unless a login cancels it.
Idempotent: a second DELETE while already pending is a
no-op 204 (no refreshed grace, no second mail). Success is
204 (no body — the client re-reads GET /v1/me, which shows
`status` + `deleted_at`).

204.description: Deletion requested; 30-day grace started (or already pending)

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

patch.summary:
PATCH /v1/me (P1-005): set the display name and/or record an
email-change intent. An email value stores `pending_email`
(validated + disposable-checked + duplicate-checked) — P1-006
verifies and swaps it. `email: null` clears a pending intent;
`display_name: null` clears the name; no fields is a no-op 200.

200.description: Updated profile

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

422.description: Validation failed (display name shape, email shape, disposable domain, email unchanged)

post.summary:
POST /v1/me/consent (P1-095): accept the current ToS + AUP
versions. The banner-clearing endpoint: a bump flips
`consent.up_to_date` false on GET /v1/me, and only this
call — with both versions equal to their current values —
clears it (audited as `user.consent_accepted`). A stale
version is 422; an already-current re-accept is a no-op 200
(the service writes nothing). Success returns the updated
profile, re-read through GET /v1/me's path.

200.description: Updated profile with cleared consent banner

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

422.description: Validation failed (a version is not the current one)

get.summary:
GET /v1/me/email-preferences (P1-103): the caller's email
prefs — `weekly_digest` + `marketing`, each defaulting to
`true` (opted in). A pure read of the user row: no write,
no audit. AuthContext, so an API key is 403 (keys are not
in the scope table — the P1-095 consent precedent); no
credential is 401.

200.description: Current email preferences

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

put.summary:
PUT /v1/me/email-preferences (P1-103): set the caller's
email prefs — `{weekly_digest?: bool, marketing?: bool}`.
At least one key must be present (empty body is 422);
unknown keys are 422; a no-op PUT (same values) is a 200
with no write and no audit; a real change is one
transaction (settings update + `user.email_prefs_updated`
audit row) and returns the updated prefs. AuthContext, so
an API key is 403 (the P1-095 consent precedent); no
credential is 401.

200.description: Updated email preferences

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

422.description: Validation failed (empty body)

get.summary:
GET /v1/me/onboarding (P1-096): the onboarding checklist
for the caller — five steps (verify email, accept ToS,
first upload, first job, optional API key), each with
`completed` + `completed_at`, plus `completed_count` /
`total_count` and `all_done` (the four required steps).
A read model over existing rows: the endpoint writes
nothing (no audit row on a read). AuthContext, so an API
key is 403 (keys are not in the scope table — the P1-095
consent precedent); no credential is 401.

200.description: Onboarding checklist with per-step completion

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

get.summary:
List the user's live sessions (P1-019, FR-A-01): device
(parsed), created, last_seen, expiry — newest first.
Revoked and expired sessions are not listed (they are
history, in `audit_logs`); the user can only act on a
live one.

200.description: Live sessions, newest first

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

delete.summary:
Revoke one of the user's sessions (P1-019, FR-A-01).
Unknown id, or an id belonging to another user → 404
`PF-2010` (no enumeration). Already revoked → no-op 204
(the session is already dead — P1-008's convention).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session id from GET /v1/me/sessions

401.description: No credential, or an invalid/expired access token (PF-1001/1010/1011)

404.description: No session with that id for this user (PF-2010)

get.summary:
Read the caller's usage (P1-080, FR-P-07): today's
bucket + the 30-day window ending today, from the
durable `usage_counters` rows. JWT callers read their
own usage; API-key callers read their key owner's
usage (the key row carries the owner id — the
extractor's `VerifiedApiKey` holds id + scopes + tier
only) and additionally get today's per-key breakdown
(`by_key`) — a JWT caller gets no `by_key` field at
all. A key needs the `jobs:read` scope (usage is read
data about the caller's own jobs, the same data
`jobs:read` already gates — ADR-0044); a key without
it is 403 `PF-1002` from the extractor before this
handler runs. No credential is 401 `PF-1001` from the
extractor. A user who used nothing gets zeros, not a
404; no audit row (a read creates nothing).

200.description: The caller's usage: today's bucket, the 30-day window ending today, and — for an API-key caller — today's per-key breakdown

401.description: Unauthenticated (no credential, bad or expired token)

403.description: An API key without the jobs:read scope (PF-1002)

post.summary:
The Razorpay webhook receiver (P1-074, FR-P-04): the
mirror of the Stripe receiver, over the Razorpay envelope
(`X-Razorpay-Signature`, `hex(hmac_sha256(webhook_secret,
raw_body))`). While `PF_FEATURE_RAZORPAY` is off the
endpoint does not exist: 404 `PF-2010`. Flag on, a bad
signature is 400 `PF-2013` (the endpoint's only 4xx);
Razorpay not configured (or Stripe active instead) is 503
`PF-5005`; every verified delivery — stored, replayed, or
ignored — is 200 with a receipt, unless the handler itself
fails (the database, or a provider call — P1-065): then it
is 500 `PF-5000` so Razorpay retries, and the redelivery
re-dispatches the still-undispatched event.

requestBody.description: The raw Razorpay event envelope — the signature covers these exact bytes

200.description: Received (stored, replayed, or ignored)

400.description: The webhook signature does not verify (PF-2013)

404.description: The Razorpay flag is off — the endpoint does not exist (PF-2010)

500.description: The handler failed (database or provider call — PF-5000); Razorpay retries

503.description: Billing is not configured (no Razorpay key, or Stripe is the active provider)

post.summary:
Receive a Stripe webhook delivery (P1-063, FR-P-04).
No auth extractor runs here by design — the provider's
signature IS the credential (the matrix row is `Ignored`).
The raw body is read as bytes: the signature covers the
exact bytes Stripe sent, and any JSON parse before the
check would break it. A bad signature is 400 `PF-2013`
(the endpoint's only 4xx); billing unconfigured is 503
`PF-5005`; every verified delivery — stored, replayed, or
ignored — is 200 with a receipt, unless the handler itself
fails (the database, or a provider call — P1-065): then it
is 500 `PF-5000` so Stripe retries, and the redelivery
re-dispatches the still-undispatched event.

requestBody.description: The raw Stripe event envelope — the signature covers these exact bytes

200.description: Received (stored, replayed, or ignored)

400.description: The webhook signature does not verify (PF-2013)

500.description: The handler failed (database or provider call — PF-5000); Stripe retries

503.description: Billing is not configured (no Stripe secret key)

AbuseIntakeRequest.description:
The abuse report intake request body (api-spec: job id,
reporter contact, reason → 201 ticket).

job_id.description:
The reported job's id, when the reporter knows it
(`None` = a general-abuse report, no job).

reason.description: What happened (1–500 chars, the P1-008 reason shape).

reporter_contact.description: The reporter's contact email (where the ack goes).

website.description:
Honeypot field — must stay blank. A human never sees
this field; a bot fills it and is dropped silently.

AbuseQueuePage.description:
One page of the queue: the api-spec pagination shape
(`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` —
`next_cursor` omitted on the last page).

items.description:
This page's reports, newest first (at most the
requested limit).

next_cursor.description:
The cursor for the next page, or `None` when this
is the last page.

AbuseReportItem.description:
One queue row as the API returns it: the stored fields,
verbatim, plus the SLA pair. `reporter_contact` is the
business record (the queue needs to reply to the
reporter) — an admin/support read, never a public one.

job_id.description: The reported job, when the report names one.

notes.description:
The resolving admin's notes — `None` until resolved
(or until a resolve carries notes).

reason.description: What happened, as filed or as the detector wrote it.

reporter_contact.description:
The reporter's contact email, as filed (intake
reports only; detector reports carry `None`).

resolution.description:
What the resolution was (`dismissed` |
`job_rejected` | `user_suspended`) — `None` until
resolved.

resolved_at.description:
When the report left the queue — `None` until
resolved.

sla_breached.description:
Whether the 72 h target was missed (a resolved
report: its `resolved_at` is past the due time; an
open or reviewing one: the clock is past it).

updated_at.description:
When the row last changed (a review pickup bumps it
too — it is not the resolution time).

user_id.description:
The reported user, when the report names one (a
detector spike always does; the public intake never
does — the reporter has no account).

AbuseReportResponse.description:
The filed report: the ticket the reporter holds (the ack
mail carries the same id).

AcceptConsentRequest.description:
The re-accept body: both versions the user accepts now.
Each must equal its current version (the same rule as
registration) — accepting a stale version cannot clear the
banner, so the handler rejects it instead of storing it.

accept_aup_version.description:
The AUP version the user accepts; must equal the
current version (`PF_AUP_CURRENT_VERSION`).

accept_tos_version.description:
The ToS version the user accepts; must equal the
current version (`PF_TOS_CURRENT_VERSION`).

AdminJobItem.description:
One row of the admin jobs list (P1-038): the job as the
dashboard shows it — identity, owner, kind, status — plus
the display prefix of the API key that created it
(`key_prefix` is `None` for a web / JWT-created job).
The prefix is the only key material this view ever shows:
never the secret, never its hash, never the full key id
as a credential (the id is a row identifier, not a
secret — the same rule as the api-keys listing).

key_id.description:
The API key that created the job, or `None` for a web
/ JWT-created job.

key_prefix.description:
The creating key's display prefix (`pf_live_…`), or
`None` for a web / JWT-created job.

AdminJobsPage.description:
The admin jobs response page: the api-spec pagination shape
(same `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` as the user
search — see [`UserSearchPage`]).

AdminUsageResponse.description:
The admin usage view: the P1-080 shape for an arbitrary
user, plus the all-time totals and — always — today's
per-key breakdown.

by_key.description:
Today's per-key breakdown — always present in the
admin view (calling key, sibling keys, and the
unattributed row for web / JWT-created jobs).
Empty when the user created nothing today.

days.description:
The 30 daily buckets ending today, oldest first.
Days with no usage are zeros, not absent rows.

today.description:
Today's bucket (the last entry of `days`, repeated
here for convenience).

totals.description:
All-time totals (every `usage_counters` row, not
just the window).

AdminUserViewResponse.description:
The support user view: profile + plan + usage + recent
jobs + live sessions + ticket notes, for one user. No field anywhere in
this shape is a secret: no password hash, no refresh
hash, no family id, no provider id, no token, no raw
user-agent string, no raw IP (ADR-0065).

recent_jobs.description:
The 10 newest jobs, newest first. Empty when the
user never created one.

sessions.description:
The live sessions (not revoked, not expired), newest
first, in the P1-019 shape. Empty when the user has
none live.

support_notes.description:
The ticket notes (P1-110): the admin-written
append-only list, oldest first. Empty when no admin
has written one — this is how the support flow reads
the notes, so there is no second GET route for them.

user_id.description: Whose view this is (the `{id}` the caller asked for).

AttestationItem.description:
One queue row as the API returns it: the stored
fields, verbatim, plus the velocity flag. `ip_hash` is
the sha256 of the client IP (NFR-42 — the raw address
is never stored); it is correlatable evidence for an
admin/support read, never a public value.

abuse_queue_url.description: The abuse queue for this user (relative reference).

flag_reasons.description:
Why the row is flagged (`["velocity"]` when
flagged, `[]` otherwise).

flagged.description: Whether this row is flagged as anomalous.

ip_hash.description: The sha256 of the client IP (NFR-42).

text_version.description: The attestation text version the client attested to.

velocity_count.description:
The user's attestation count in the 24 h window
ending at this row's `created_at` (inclusive).

AttestationsPage.description:
One page of the queue: the api-spec pagination shape
(`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` —
`next_cursor` omitted on the last page).

items.description:
This page's attestations, newest first (at most the
requested limit).

next_cursor.description:
The cursor for the next page, or `None` when this
is the last page.

AuditLogItem.description:
One audit row as the query API returns it: the stored
fields, verbatim. `before`/`after` carry hashes, never
raw PII (NFR-42 — the writers' contract, see the audit
service); this endpoint does not redact, it only reads.

actor_user_id.description:
The acting user, if any (anonymous or system events
carry `None`).

after.description: State after the action (hashes, never raw PII).

before.description: State before the action, if meaningful.

reason.description: Why, when the action needs a reason.

target_id.description: The target's id (a user UUID once it exists).

AuditPage.description:
One page of the audit trail: the api-spec pagination
shape (`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` —
`next_cursor` omitted on the last page).

items.description:
This page's rows, newest first (at most the
requested limit).

next_cursor.description:
The cursor for the next page, or `None` when this
is the last page.

CatalogDriftReport.description:
The drift report: one line per plan plus the counts. This is
the ticket's AC — the report is produced by every sync run,
returned by the admin endpoint, and logged by the nightly job.
Serializable so the endpoint can return it as JSON unchanged.

plans.description:
One line per plan, in catalog order (cheapest first, as
the caller passes them).

ChangeKind.description: Which way a plan change moves, by catalog amount.

CheckoutRequestBody.description:
The checkout request body: the plan to buy. The price
comes from the catalog, never from the request.

CheckoutResponse.description:
The 200 body for a purchase or an upgrade: the hosted
session, plus the proration preview when the buyer already
holds a plan (`null` for a first purchase — there is no
old plan to prorate from).

oneOf.description:
The upgrade's proration preview (`null` for a first
purchase). Old idempotency rows (P1-062) carry no key
— it defaults to `null` on read.

ComponentHealth.description:
One readiness component: a name, up/down, a safe detail
string, and the probe latency in milliseconds (P0-066).
`detail` never contains the database URL or credentials.
`latency_ms` is measured by the probe itself, from probe start
to the outcome — including the timeout path, so a slow
component reports a large latency instead of a missing one.
A sub-millisecond probe honestly reports 0.

ConfirmEmailChangeRequest.description:
The confirm-email-change request body (api-spec: token →
204). Same shape as [`VerifyEmailRequest`] — a different
type on purpose: the two endpoints consume different token
purposes, and sharing the request type would invite sharing
the handler.

token.description: The raw token from the change-confirmation link.

ConsentStatus.description:
The consent section of GET /v1/me (and of the re-accept
response): the versions the user accepted, the versions
current in config, and whether the user is up to date.
`None` accepted versions mean "never accepted" — stale by
definition, so a pre-P1-095 account shows the banner until
it re-accepts once.

aup_version.description: The AUP version the user accepted (`None` = never).

tos_version.description: The ToS version the user accepted (`None` = never).

up_to_date.description:
False when either accepted version is older than (or
missing against) its current version — the banner.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: The POST body: a human label + the scopes the key may use.

name.description: Human label, e.g. `"CI deploy"` — shown in listings.

scopes.description:
At least one of `jobs:write`, `jobs:read`,
`webhooks:manage`; no duplicates.

CreateApiKeyResponse.description:
The creation response — the ONLY place the full secret ever
appears. Everything else about the key (listings, audit)
shows the prefix + last4, never this.

id.description: The key id — the revoke/rotate target.

secret.description: The full secret (`pf_live_` + 32 chars). Shown once.

DayUsage.description:
One day's usage: the counters for one UTC date. A day
with no row reads as zeros — the row only exists once
the user has used something that day.

date.description: The UTC date this bucket covers (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

EmailPrefs.description:
The two email prefs, each defaulting to opted in.
Serialized with the same key names the settings jsonb
carries, so the response is the stored shape.

EnforcementResponse.description:
The HTTP shape for a warn/terminate: the user + the rung
that ran + what it did.

already.description: The account was already in the target state.

Entitlements.description:
The seven entitlements of a plan, parsed from the
`plans.entitlements` jsonb. All numbers are `i64`:
`max_bytes` for Business is 4 GiB, past `i32::MAX`.

concurrency.description: Concurrent running jobs for the user.

daily_images.description: Images per UTC day (0 = no images — fail closed).

daily_video_seconds.description: Video seconds per UTC day (0 = no video).

features.description:
Named feature flags (`api_keys`, `webhooks`, `batch`).
`priority_lane` is NOT a map entry — it reads the
`lane` field (see [`Entitlements::grants`]).

lane.description: Which lane the plan's jobs run in.

result_ttl_hours.description: How long a finished result is kept, in hours.

FieldError.description:
One failed field in a 422 validation rejection (P0-101).

Serialized as an element of `Problem.field_errors`. The `message`
is generic by design — it never echoes the offending value — so
the list is safe to show in production, unlike `detail` (which
stays the variant's static safe text in production).

code.description:
Stable machine code, e.g. `invalid_email` — one per rule,
documented where the rule lives (`detag-validator`).

field.description: The request field that failed, e.g. `email`.

message.description: Human-readable message, e.g. `must be a valid email address`.

ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
The forgot-password request body: the email that may (or
may not) have an account.

email.description: The email to (maybe) send a reset link to.

ImpersonateResponse.description:
The impersonation response (P1-010): a 15-minute scoped
token that acts as the target user, plus the two ids the
console needs for the banner — who is acting, and as whom.
There is no refresh token and no session row behind it:
the token dies at `exp` and cannot be renewed.

access_token.description:
The HS256 access token (15 min), carrying
`impersonator_id` in its claims.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires (900).

impersonator_id.description:
The admin who is impersonating (the token's
`impersonator_id` claim).

Invoice.description:
One invoice, as `GET /v1/billing/invoices` lists it. Amounts are
the provider's smallest unit (paise for INR); `status` is the
provider's own string (`paid` / `open` / `void` / ...), kept opaque
on purpose — each provider spells these differently.

amount.description: Total in the smallest currency unit.

created_at.description: When the provider created the invoice.

download_url.description:
The Stripe-hosted PDF download, when the provider offers
one (P1-068: the spec's "stripe-hosted download URLs" —
`hosted_url` is the page, this is the file).

hosted_url.description: The hosted invoice page, when the provider offers one.

number.description: The human invoice number, when the provider assigns one.

KeyUsage.description:
One key's usage for today: the counts plus the
identity the caller shows. `key_id` is `None` for the
unattributed row (web / JWT-created jobs).

images.description: Image jobs created today by the key.

key_id.description: The key, or `None` for unattributed jobs.

key_prefix.description:
The key's display prefix (`pf_live_…`), or `None`
for the unattributed row.

video_jobs.description: Video jobs created today by the key.

video_seconds.description:
Video seconds used today by the key — 0 until
Phase 2 records usage at job create/completion
(see the module docs); read `video_jobs` for the
count, never this field for seconds.

Lane.description:
Which lane a plan's jobs run in. Unknown values read as
`standard` (fail closed — the priority lane is the
higher-privilege one).

LoginRequest.description:
The login request body (api-spec: email, password → 200
access token + refresh cookie).

email.description: The email address (trimmed + lowercased before lookup).

password.description: The password (never trimmed, never logged, never stored).

LoginResponse.description:
The login response body: the access token + its lifetime.
The refresh token is NOT in the body — it travels as the
httpOnly `detag_refresh` cookie (set by the handler).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires (900).

OnboardingChecklist.description:
The checklist response: the five steps in display order,
raw completion counts, and whether the required steps are
all complete.

all_done.description:
True when the four required steps are complete — the
optional API-key step never blocks this.

completed_count.description: Completed steps (all five counted, optional included).

steps.description: The five steps, in display order.

OnboardingStep.description:
One checklist step: a stable id the web keys on, a human
title, whether the step is optional, and its completion
state. `completed_at` is null until the step completes.

completed.description: Whether the step is complete right now.

completed_at.description: When the step completed (`None` until then).

optional.description:
True only for `create_api_key` — the optional step
never blocks `all_done`.

title.description: Human title for the web checklist.

PatchProfileRequest.description:
The PATCH body: each field is `Option<Option<..>>` —
absent = leave unchanged, `null` = clear, a value = set.
(`#[serde(default)]` supplies the absent case; the custom
deserializer supplies the null case — see above.)

display_name.description: The display name to set (`null` clears it).

email.description:
The new email address — records an email-change intent
(`null` clears a pending intent). P1-006 verifies it.

PlanEdit.description:
One plan update, keyed by `code`. Absent fields are
unchanged — only `entitlements`, when present, must be
the full object.

amount.description: New price in paise (`>= 0`); Free must stay 0.

currency.description: New ISO currency code (three uppercase letters).

stripe_price_id.description:
New Stripe price id: a string sets it, `null` clears
it, absent leaves it unchanged. Free takes no price.
The `deserialize_with` keeps `null` distinct from
missing — plain serde derive collapses the two (the
same trap `services/profile.rs` documents for its
PATCH body).

PlanEntitlementsEdit.description:
The seven entitlements of one plan edit. Every field is
required when the object is present — a partial
entitlements object is a 422, never a merge (the
fail-closed parse would read a missing key as 0, so a
half-written object could silently ungrant a quota).

concurrency.description: Concurrent running jobs for the user.

features.description: Named feature flags (only the known names, bool only).

result_ttl_hours.description: How long a finished result is kept, in hours.

PlanResponse.description: The plan section of the profile.

amount.description: The price in the smallest currency unit (paise for INR).

PlanSyncResult.description: One plan's line in the drift report.

detail.description:
Human detail — what was created / adopted / archived,
or the provider failure for `Failed`.

old_price_archived.description:
True when this run archived the previous price. A
replacement whose old price was already inactive (or
missing) archives nothing — the count of archived prices
reads this flag, not the action.

previous_price_id.description: The price id this run replaced, when it replaced one.

price_id.description: The price id after the sync, when the plan has one.

product_id.description: The product id after the sync, when the plan has one.

PlanView.description:
One plan, as the editor shows it and returns it: the
stored row with the entitlements parsed (canonical — the
seven keys, so a stored jsonb with extra keys round-trips
as the effective entitlements, never as raw jsonb).

amount.description: Price in paise (`amount` in the DB).

stripe_price_id.description:
Stripe price id, or null when the plan has no price
(Free).

PlansResponse.description: The catalog response: all plans, cheapest first.

PortalSession.description: What `create_portal` returns: the hosted billing-portal URL.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem body, as served by the api (`application/problem+json`).

detail.description:
Human-readable detail. In production this is always the variant's
static safe detail — never caller-supplied internals.

field_errors.description:
Per-field failures (P0-101). Present only on validation
rejections; omitted otherwise, so every other error body keeps
exactly the RFC 7807 fields the contract test locks.

request_id.description:
Echoed request id (UUIDv7); omitted when the caller has none yet
(request-id middleware lands in P0-019).

upgrade_url.description:
Plan-matrix link (P1-054, FR-P-06). Present ONLY on quota
denials (`PF-3001` / `PF-3002` / `PF-3008`) — the
`{PF_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/plans` URL the client links when it
renders the 429. Omitted everywhere else, so every other
error body keeps exactly the RFC 7807 fields the contract
test locks.

ProfileResponse.description:
The profile response: the user + the current plan +
today's quota snapshot. The password hash is never here
(P1-003); the pending email IS shown (the client needs to
know a change is pending — it is the user's own address).

consent.description:
The consent state (P1-095): the ToS + AUP versions the
user accepted, the versions current in config, and
whether the user is up to date — `up_to_date: false` is
the re-accept banner (POST /v1/me/consent clears it).

deleted_at.description:
When the deletion was requested (set only during the
30-day deletion grace, P1-007 — the account is purged
30 days after this timestamp unless a login cancels it).

email.description: The current (verified or not) email address.

email_verified_at.description: When the email was verified (None until then).

pending_email.description:
A pending email change (P1-005 records it; P1-006
verifies + swaps it). None when no change is pending.

plan.description:
The current plan (the live subscription's plan, else
Free).

quota.description: Today's quota snapshot (daily limits vs today's usage).

ProrationPreview.description:
What a plan change costs, and when it takes effect. The
wire shape of the checkout response's `proration` field
(and of the downgrade 202 body).

charge_paise.description:
New-plan value for the remainder (paise). Zero for a
downgrade — nothing moves now.

credit_paise.description:
Unused old-plan value returned to the buyer (paise).
Zero for a downgrade — nothing moves now.

effective_at.description:
When the new plan takes effect: now for an upgrade,
the period end for a downgrade.

net_paise.description:
`charge - credit`: what the change costs beyond the
plan price the checkout already collects. Never
negative for an upgrade; zero for a downgrade.

QuotaBucketResponse.description:
One quota bucket: the daily limit, today's usage, and
what is left.

QuotaGrantRequest.description:
The grant request: at least one amount, a TTL, and the
reason the audit carries verbatim.

images.description:
Extra daily images (optional — at least one of the
two amounts must be present).

reason.description:
Why the grant is made (1–500 characters after
trimming; the audit carries it verbatim).

ttl_hours.description: How long the grant lives, in hours (1–168).

video_seconds.description:
Extra daily video-seconds (optional — at least one of
the two amounts must be present).

QuotaGrantResponse.description: The grant, as the API returns it.

images.description: The extra daily images (`None` = this grant adds none).

video_seconds.description: The extra daily video-seconds (`None` = this grant adds none).

QuotaResponse.description: Today's quota snapshot: the two daily buckets.

Readiness.description:
Overall readiness: `"ok"` only when every component is ok (and
at least one component was checked — an empty report is
`"degraded"`, never `"ok"`).

ReasonRequest.description:
The body for admin actions that need a reason (suspend,
impersonate): the reason is required — an admin action
without one is not auditable. Shared by every such action
so the shape (and the validation) has one definition.

reason.description:
Why the action is taken (1–500 characters after
trimming; the audit carries it verbatim).

RecentJobView.description:
One recent job: id, kind, status, and the timestamps.
Deliberately absent: `params` (may carry storage keys),
`webhook_url`, `idempotency_key`, `error` (may carry
internal detail), `upload_id`, `key_id` — support needs
to see that a job ran and how it ended, not its inputs.

finished_at.description: When the job finished (`None` = not finished).

RefundChecklistResponse.description: The 200 body for a refund request.

checklist.description: The four dashboard steps, all `done: false`.

plan_code.description: The plan the subscription is on.

required_fields.description: The fields the dashboard refund form needs.

status.description:
The row's status now — any status may be refunded,
including already-canceled.

subscription_id.description: The subscription the refund is for.

RefundChecklistStep.description:
One checklist step: what support does in the dashboard,
in order. `done` is always `false` — the API cannot know
what a human did in the dashboard, and a `done: true`
would be a lie.

detail.description: What support does at this step.

done.description: Whether the step is done — always `false` (see above).

step.description: The step number, 1–4, in the order support does them.

RefundGuidance.description:
Where a refund happens: the Stripe dashboard, never this
API.

dashboard_url.description:
The Stripe dashboard URL for the subscription (or
the subscriptions list when the row carries no
provider id).

note.description:
What support does there: cancel the Stripe
subscription too, and issue any refund on the latest
invoice or payment.

RefundRequiredField.description:
One field the dashboard refund form needs: the value
where the API knows it, `null` where only support knows
it (a null with no guess is honest — a guessed id would
be a lie).

field.description: The field name, as the dashboard form names it.

value.description: The value, or `null` when only support knows it.

RegisterRequest.description:
The register request body (api-spec: email, password,
accept_tos_version + accept_aup_version → 201 user +
verification email sent).

accept_aup_version.description:
The AUP version the user accepted (P1-095); must equal
the current version (`PF_AUP_CURRENT_VERSION`, default
"v1") — the same rule as the ToS version, so a
registration records both consents at once.

accept_tos_version.description:
The ToS version the user accepted; must equal the current
version (`PF_TOS_CURRENT_VERSION`, default "v1").

email.description: The email address (trimmed + lowercased before storage).

password.description:
The password (never trimmed, never logged, never stored —
only its Argon2id hash is).

ResendVerificationRequest.description:
The resend-verification request body (P1-002: no route in
the original spec — added by this ticket, see the handler).

email.description: The email to (maybe) re-send a verification mail to.

ResetPasswordRequest.description:
The reset-password request body: the token from the reset
link + the new password.

new_password.description:
The new password (min 12 chars — the P1-001 rule;
strength + blocklist land with P1-026).

token.description: The raw token from the reset link.

ResolveAbuseReportRequest.description:
The resolve body: the action, the admin's reason
(required — an admin action without one is not
auditable, the P1-008 precedent), and optional notes
stored on the report.

action.description: What to do with the report.

notes.description:
Notes for the report row (1–500 characters when
present).

reason.description:
Why the action is taken (1–500 characters after
trimming; the audit carries it verbatim).

ResolveAction.description:
The resolve action (P1-090): the three terminal actions
from the spec, plus the review pickup that makes the
`reviewing` state reachable.

ScheduledChangeResponse.description:
The 202 body for a downgrade: no session — the change is
scheduled, and the buyer keeps the old plan until
`effective_at`.

effective_at.description:
When the new plan takes effect (the current period
end, or now when the row carries no period end).

from_plan_code.description: The plan the subscription moves from.

plan_code.description: The plan the subscription moves to at `effective_at`.

proration.description:
The downgrade's proration preview: all legs zero
(nothing is charged now), `kind: downgrade`.

scheduled.description:
Always `true`: this body is a scheduled change, not a
session. The flag is what the idempotency replay keys
on to tell the two wire bodies apart.

created_at.description: When the session was created (the login that minted it).

device.description:
The parsed device label, e.g. `"Chrome on macOS"`
(never the raw User-Agent string).

expires_at.description: When the refresh token expires (30 days from login).

ip_hash.description:
sha256 of the client IP at login (a hash, not PII) —
`None` when the session row has no device record.

last_seen.description:
Last time the session was presented (the refresh flow
advances it, throttled — P1-019). `None` for rows
created before the migration (no activity recorded).

SupportCancelResponse.description: The 200 body for a support cancel.

changed.description:
Whether this call moved the row (`false` = it was
already canceled: no write, no audit, no mail).

plan_code.description: The plan the subscription was on.

subscription_id.description: The subscription that was canceled (or already was).

SyncAction.description: What the sync did for one plan.

TicketNote.description:
One ticket note: the JSON object stored in
`users.support_notes`.

author_role.description:
The author's role at write time (`admin` — only
admins can write today, recorded anyway so the history
survives a role change).

created_at.description: When it was written (the app clock).

id.description: The note id (uuidv7, from the app clock).

TicketNoteRequest.description:
The note request: the body, nothing else (the target is
the path id, the author is the caller).

body.description: The note text (1–2000 characters after trimming).

TicketNotesResponse.description:
The notes, as the API returns them: the user + the full
list after the append, oldest first.

notes.description:
The full list, oldest first (the appended note is
last).

UpdateEmailPreferencesRequest.description:
The PUT body: the prefs to change. At least one must be
present (an empty body is 422); unknown fields are
rejected (a typo'd key must not silently do nothing).

marketing.description: Opt marketing mail in (`true`) or out (`false`).

weekly_digest.description: Opt the weekly digest in (`true`) or out (`false`).

UpdatePlansRequest.description:
The PUT body: per-plan updates plus the codes to remove.
Both fields are optional; a body with neither is a
no-op 200 returning the unchanged catalog.

remove.description: Plan codes to delete (each guarded: no active subs).

UsageResponse.description:
The usage response: today's bucket, the 30-day window,
and — only for an API-key caller — today's per-key
breakdown.

by_key.description:
Today's per-key breakdown — present only when the
caller authenticated with an API key; absent for
JWT callers. Empty when the caller created nothing
today.

days.description:
The 30 daily buckets ending today, oldest first.
Days with no usage are zeros, not absent rows.

today.description:
Today's bucket (the last entry of `days`, repeated
here for convenience).

UsageTotals.description:
A user's all-time usage totals: the sums over every
`usage_counters` row the user has, not just the 30-day
window.

UserPlanView.description:
The plan section: the effective plan + the live
subscription's dates. `code` is always present (`"free"`
when there is no live subscription — the `UserSearchRow`
precedent); the other three are `None`/`false` exactly
then. Deliberately absent: the provider customer and
provider subscription ids — support works in Detag, not
in the provider dashboard (the refund tool, P1-108, owns
the deep link).

cancel_at_period_end.description:
The subscription ends at the period end (`false` =
renews, or no live subscription).

current_period_end.description:
When the current period ends (`None` = no live
subscription).

status.description:
The live subscription's status (`trialing` /
`active`) — `None` when there is no live subscription.

UserProfileView.description:
The profile section: the account, as support sees it.
Every field is already visible on the P1-009 search row
(`UserSearchRow`) except `pending_email` (an in-flight
email change — support-relevant for recovery) and
`deleted_at` (the deletion grace — support-relevant for
"where did the account go"). Deliberately absent:
`password_hash` (the credential), `settings` (the user's
private prefs blob — the support workflow never needs it),
`revoked_before` (an internal revocation epoch).

aup_version.description: The AUP version the user accepted (`None` = never).

deleted_at.description: The deletion request time (`None` = not deleting).

email_verified_at.description: When the email was verified (`None` = never).

id.description: The user id (the `{id}` the caller asked for).

pending_email.description:
The address an email change is moving to (`None` =
no change in flight).

tos_version.description: The ToS version the user accepted (`None` = never).

updated_at.description: When the account was last updated.

UserResponse.description:
The register response: the created user, without the password
hash (there is no field for it — the type makes the leak
impossible, not just unlikely).

UserSearchItem.description:
One row of the admin user search (P1-009): the user as the
dashboard shows them — identity, status, plan, and today's
usage. `plan` is the plan code (`free` when the user has no
live subscription); `usage_today` is the UTC day's counters
(zeros when the user has used nothing today).

UserSearchPage.description:
The search response page: the api-spec pagination shape
(`{"items": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` — `next_cursor`
omitted on the last page). Built from core's `Page` (the
keyset math lives there); this struct exists so the
response has an OpenAPI schema (`Page<T>` is generic and
carries no `ToSchema`).

UserUsageView.description:
The usage section: today's bucket + the all-time totals.
The 30-day window lives at `GET /v1/admin/usage/{id}`
(P1-081) — the support view carries the summary, not the
window, so one screen answers "how much has this user
used?".

today.description: Today's bucket (images + video seconds used today).

totals.description:
All-time totals (every `usage_counters` row, not
just the window).

token.description: The raw token from the verification link.

WebhookReceipt.description:
The receipt the endpoint answers with (200, replay or not).
Stripe ignores the body; the shape exists so the OpenAPI
spec documents a real response instead of an empty one.

received.description:
The event was received (stored, replayed, or ignored —
all three are a receipt, never an error).
